sub_scenario.family: rapid live troubleshooting leadership versus careful asynchronous incident analysis
sub_scenario.one_line: railway rolling-stock reliability planner: recommend reliability action without withdrawal authority

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the failure linkage board and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The fleet diary review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I explained a completed door-fault review to the depot team.
Was a withdrawal decision still open?
No, the units had returned to service.
Someone new shadowed me in the maintenance planning cell this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the service disruptions into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
I did a standard pass over the fleet diary records this morning.
Any exceptions in there?
None worth a note.
I added a maintenance window to the fleet diary.
Did that identify a failing component?
No, it was a schedule entry.
I archived last cycle's notes on the fleet diary and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The service-recovery call starts at 15:45, and platform allocations lock at 16:05.
Can either time move?
No, dispatch has fixed both.
A vendor call about the failure linkage board ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the maintenance planning cell checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the service disruptions.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the fleet diary records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
I closed a routine service disruptions cycle without surprises.
Follow-up needed?
A note for the next cycle, nothing more.
I sketched next week's plan for the service disruptions before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the failure linkage board updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The depot comparison has a 15:30 delivery slot, and the call roster has separate reliability-note and withdrawal-authorization fields.
Are those arrangements confirmed?
Yes, the delivery slot and both roster fields are booked.
I compared two options for the fleet diary tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the maintenance planning cell handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
How should I define my part in the next recovery call?

ev_A.fact: For recurring door faults in February, I compared a week of telemetry, repair histories, and driver reports, isolated one actuator series, and scheduled targeted replacements that reduced cancellations.

ev_B.fact: On an April disruption bridge, I led the fleet recommendation from two similar door reports and urged withdrawal of the whole class; the controller followed it, but later telemetry showed a platform transmitter fault, so the class withdrawal and spare-train deployment had been unnecessary.

E1.fact: The service-recovery call starts at 15:45, and platform allocations lock at 16:05.

E2.fact: The depot comparison has a 15:30 delivery slot, and the call roster has separate reliability-note and withdrawal-authorization fields.
